name: IDE
summary: Coding agents reach developers inside their editor, either through editor-specific extensions or through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). ACP, created by Zed, standardizes how an editor talks to an agent: local agents run as subprocesses and speak JSON-RPC over stdio, reusing MCP's JSON types where possible. Any ACP agent can then work in any ACP editor.
facts: JSON-RPC over stdio; remote over HTTP or WebSocket in progress
Zed, JetBrains IDEs, VS Code and Neovim via extensions, Emacs
Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode and more
Protocol v1 stable; v2 in draft (2026-07-20)
Agent Client Protocol (ACP) for editor ↔ agent
goodFor: Coding agents that edit files with diffs and review
Shipping one agent to many editors
watchOut: Remote-agent support is still in progress
